oneliner.t: Republican nominee: a Phoenix internist and nuclear cardiologist, Navy veteran, founder of the American Islamic Forum for Democracy and former vice chair of the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom; unopposed on the July 21, 2026 primary ballot (39,431 votes) after Jerone Davison's removal, in his second run for AZ-04 after finishing second in the 2024 GOP primary.

born.note: Exact date from Wikipedia; Ohio and 1967 also in Pipes's profile.

hometown.t: Neenah, Wisconsin (raised in Appleton until age 6, then Neenah)

upbringing.t: Born in Canton, Ohio, to a cardiologist father and a pharmacist mother who emigrated from the Middle East in the 1960s (Wikipedia says from Beirut, Lebanon, in 1963; Pipes and his campaign say they fled Syria), he grew up in Appleton and Neenah, Wisconsin. He earned a B.S. at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (1988) and an M.D. at the Medical College of Wisconsin (1992) on a Navy scholarship. He served in the Navy, including as a staff internist in the Office of the Attending Physician for Congress, leaving as a lieutenant commander in 1999, then moved to the Phoenix area and joined his father's practice. He lives in Scottsdale with his wife and three children.

profile.office_years_note: Appointed USCIRF commissioner 2012, reappointed 2014 (two two-year terms). Maricopa County Board of Health membership (since 2005, per Wikipedia) not counted.

career.role: Navy medical officer (scholarship, residency, staff internist Office of the Attending Physician, USS El Paso, Bethesda chief resident); Lieutenant Commander

platform.t: Blames federal spending under Democratic leadership for inflation; would introduce a bill on his first day to suspend the federal gas tax temporarily.

Criticizes the ACA for consolidation and higher prices; favors selling insurance across state lines, price transparency, 'most favored nation' drug pricing, site-neutral pricing and anti-consolidation oversight of private-equity-owned and large health systems.
Attributes affordability problems mainly to inflation; would limit foreign-entity purchases of U.S. homes.

Supports growth to compete with China but with community guardrails: developers pay their own power and infrastructure costs; a federal-state framework offering property-tax relief to host communities.
Supports a balanced-budget amendment and spending and regulatory cuts; 2024 survey backed a 15% flat tax; signed the Taxpayer Protection Pledge.

More resources for border agents; seal the border and strengthen vetting before addressing those already here; restore military readiness and oppose 'social engineering' in the ranks; calls China a priority threat and urges 'maximum pressure' on Iran.
School choice / 'educational freedom,' state and local control.

research_notes: 2024 GOP primary: Kelly Cooper 32.0% (18,902), Jasser 27.0% (15,929), Dave Giles 23.0%, Jerone Davison 18.1% (Ballotpedia). Wikipedia's phrasing 'lost to Kelly Cooper' refers to that primary. The Arizona Medical Association's 2025 item says he 'ran for the same seat in 2022'; the record shows 2024, so that line is treated as the association's error and not rated as his claim. Ballotpedia's 2026 section (five-way Aug 4 primary) is stale. Endorsements in 2024 (Ballotpedia): Jan Brewer, Jon Kyl, Rick Santorum. Documented relationship: Daniel Pipes (Middle East Forum) wrote in his 2024 endorsement op-ed that he has helped fund Jasser's organizations; that is a disclosed tie to AIFD, not a campaign contribution, and no MEF money to the campaign was found. Critics' characterizations (CAIR, Media Matters) and supporters' (Pipes) are opinion and are not scored. Parents' and father's records are not his.
